   407	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   408	theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_one_sub_of_isProj {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   409	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
   410	    (B C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   411	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a)) (hC : ∀ x a, IsProj (C x a))
   412	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a))
   413	    (hAC : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (C x a)) :
   414	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * B x a))) -
   415	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
   416	      Real.sqrt (1 - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   417	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) := by
   418	  have hpt : ∀ x, (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) -
   419	      (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * B x a))) =
   420	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (C x a * (1 - B x a))) := by
   421	    intro x
   422	    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   423	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   424	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   425	  rw [abs_sub_comm, ← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
   426	  have h1B : ∀ x a, IsProj (1 - B x a) := fun x a => (hB x a).one_sub
   427	  have hA1B : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (1 - B x a) := fun x a =>
   428	    (Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAB x a)
   429	  have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ A C
   430	    (fun x a => 1 - B x a) ψ hC hAC
   431	  have hsecond : avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
   432	      stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (1 - B x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a)) =
   433	      1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) := by
   434	    have hx : ∀ x, (∑ a,
   435	        stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (1 - B x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a)) =
   436	        1 - ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a) := by
   437	      intro x
   438	      rw [← sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   439	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   440	      rw [stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (h1B x a) (hA1B x a)]
   441	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   442	    rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ hx, avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ]
   443	  have hfirst : Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   444	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))) ≤ 1 := by
   445	    rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
   446	    exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
   447	      (avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A C ψ hμ hψ hC hAC)
   448	  rw [hsecond] at hcs
   449	  calc
   450	    _ ≤ _ := hcs
   451	    _ ≤ 1 * Real.sqrt (1 - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   452	          ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) :=
   453	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hfirst (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   454	    _ = _ := one_mul _
   455	
   456	/-- The deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate with the product family
   457	`C B` supplied as one family `CB`, which is convenient when the product is
   458	formed on a local space before being placed. -/
   459	theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_one_sub_of_isProj' {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   460	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
   461	    (B C CB : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   462	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a)) (hC : ∀ x a, IsProj (C x a))
   463	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a))
   464	    (hAC : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (C x a))
   465	    (hCB : ∀ x a, CB x a = C x a * B x a) :
   466	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * CB x a)) -
   467	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
   468	      Real.sqrt (1 - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   469	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) := by
   470	  rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by rw [hCB]]
   471	  exact abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_one_sub_of_isProj μ A B C ψ hμ hψ hB hC hAB hAC
   472	
   473	/-- Inserting an arbitrary operator family `W` after a projection family `R`
   474	commuting with the effects of `A` costs at most the square root of the
   475	averaged squared norms of `W ψ`. -/
   476	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj {X α ι : Type*}
   477	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X)
   478	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (R W : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   479	    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
   480	    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a)) :
   481	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (R x a * W x a)))| ≤
   482	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   483	        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (W x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   484	  have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ A R W ψ hR hAR
   485	  have hfirst : Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   486	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a))) ≤ 1 := by
   487	    rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
   488	    exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
   489	      (avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR)
   490	  have hsecond : avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
   491	      stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (W x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a)) ≤
   492	      avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (W x a) ψ‖ ^ 2) :=
   493	    avgOver_mono μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ =>
   494	      stateQForm_le_norm_sq_of_le_one _ (measurement_effect_le_one (A x) a)
   495	  calc
   496	    _ ≤ _ := hcs
   497	    _ ≤ 1 * Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   498	          ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (W x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)) :=
   499	      mul_le_mul hfirst (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hsecond) (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   500	        zero_le_one
   501	    _ = _ := one_mul _
   502	
   503	/-- The mirror image of the preceding estimate: an operator family `W`
   504	commuting with the effects of `A`, inserted before a commuting projection
   505	family `R`, costs at most the square root of the averaged squared norms of
   506	`Wᴴ ψ`. -/
   507	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj' {X α ι : Type*}
   508	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X)
   509	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (W R : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   510	    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
   511	    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a))
   512	    (hAW : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a)) :
   513	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a * R x a)))| ≤
   514	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   515	        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (W x a)ᴴ ψ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   516	  have hrw : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a * R x a)) =
   517	      stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (R x a * (W x a)ᴴ)) := by
   518	    intro x a
   519	    have hAWH : Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a)ᴴ := by
   520	      have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (hAW x a).eq
   521	      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
   522	        measurement_effect_hermitian] at h
   523	      exact h.symm
   524	    rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a * R x a)),
   525	      Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
   526	      measurement_effect_hermitian, (hR x a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   527	    congr 1
   528	    exact ((hAR x a).mul_right hAWH).eq.symm
   529	  rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hrw x a]
   530	  exact abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj μ A R
   531	    (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
   532	
   533	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Witnesses
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.Calculus
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# The ordered point product on a single placement
     6	
     7	The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
     8	with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
     9	The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
    10	families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
    11	joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
    12	triangle inequality twice.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
    18	`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
    32	between the two members of each pair. -/
    33	theorem Placement.exists_isOpposite (p : Placement) :
    34	    ∃ q : Placement, p.IsOpposite q ∧ q.IsOpposite p := by
    35	  cases p with
    36	  | AA' => exact ⟨.BA'', trivial, trivial⟩
    37	  | BA'' => exact ⟨.AA', trivial, trivial⟩
    38	  | BB' => exact ⟨.AB'', trivial, trivial⟩
    39	  | AB'' => exact ⟨.BB', trivial, trivial⟩
    40	
    41	/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
    42	`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
    43	theorem CombinedPointsWitness.orderedZX_dist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    44	    {ε δ : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
    45	    (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) (p : Placement) :
    46	    opFamilyDistSq
    47	        (uniformDistribution
    48	          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    49	        (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    50	        (fun xz ab => S.place p
    51	          ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    52	            (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    53	        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * δ := by
    54	  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hqp⟩ := p.exists_isOpposite
    55	  have htri := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le
    56	    (uniformDistribution
    57	      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    58	    (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    59	    (fun xz ab => S.place q ((points.Q q.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    60	    (fun xz ab => S.place p
    61	      ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    62	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    63	    S.psiHat δ δ (points.self_consistent p q hpq)
    64	    (points.consistent_ZX q p hqp)
    65	  linarith
    66	
    67	end
    68	
    69	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineMeasurement
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Placement calculus on the expanded state
     5	
     6	This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
     7	combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
     8	opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
     9	pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
    10	to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
    11	state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
    12	`def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1003-1030`, paper
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.  The
    19	EPR-exchange invariance is the element `U_σ U_θ` of
    20	`lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer`, blueprint
    21	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1032-1130`, which needs no
    22	symmetry of the strategy; its use for `lem:qld-4-10` is analyzed in
    23	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    27	
    28	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    29	
    30	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    31	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    32	
    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    36	
    37	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    38	
    39	/-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/
    40	
    41	/-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
    42	`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
    43	theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    44	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AA'.side)) :
    45	    S.place .AA' O =
    46	      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    47	        (heteroKron O
    48	          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
    49	            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    50	  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm
    51	
    52	/-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
    53	`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
    54	theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
    56	    S.place .BA'' O =
    57	      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    58	        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
    59	          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    60	  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_right S O).symm
    61	
    62	/-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
    63	`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
    64	theorem place_AB''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AB''.side)) :
    66	    S.place .AB'' O =
    67	      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    68	        (heteroKron O
    69	          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
    70	            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    71	  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm
    72	
    73	/-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
    74	`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
    75	theorem place_BB'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    76	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BB'.side)) :
    77	    S.place .BB' O =
    78	      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    79	        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
    80	          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    81	  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_right S O).symm
    82	
    83	/-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
    84	theorem reindexOp_conjTranspose {ι κ : Type*} (e : ι ≃ κ) (M : Op κ) :
    85	    reindexOp e Mᴴ = (reindexOp e M)ᴴ := by
    86	  ext i j
    87	  rfl
    88	
    89	/-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
    90	theorem reindexOp_nonneg {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
    91	    (e : ι ≃ κ) {M : Op κ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    92	    0 ≤ reindexOp e M := by
    93	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
    94	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite κ
    95	  rw [Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef] at hM ⊢
    96	  exact hM.submatrix e.symm.symm
    97	
    98	/-! ## The placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism -/
    99	
   100	set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
   101	/-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
   102	theorem place_mul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   103	    ∀ (p : Placement) (A B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
   104	      S.place p (A * B) = S.place p A * S.place p B
   105	  | .AA', A, B => by
   106	      classical
   107	      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq,
   108	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
   109	      all_goals rfl
   110	  | .BA'', A, B => by
   111	      classical
   112	      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq,
   113	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   114	        mul_one, mul_one]
   115	      all_goals rfl
   116	  | .BB', A, B => by
   117	      classical
   118	      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq,
   119	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   120	        mul_one, mul_one]
   121	      all_goals rfl
   122	  | .AB'', A, B => by
   123	      classical
   124	      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq,
   125	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
   126	      all_goals rfl
   127	
   128	/-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
   129	space. -/
   130	theorem place_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :
   131	    S.place p (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) = 1 := by
   132	  ext i j
   133	  cases p <;>
   134	    · simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.one_apply, Prod.ext_iff]
   135	      split_ifs <;> simp_all
   136	
   137	/-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators. -/
   138	theorem place_finsetSum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {γ : Type*}
   139	    (s : Finset γ) (O : γ → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   140	    S.place p (∑ x ∈ s, O x) = ∑ x ∈ s, S.place p (O x) := by
   141	  ext i j
   142	  cases p <;>
   143	    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul,
   144	      Finset.mul_sum]
   145	
   146	/-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
   147	theorem place_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   148	    ∀ (p : Placement) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
   149	      S.place p Aᴴ = (S.place p A)ᴴ
   150	  | .AA', A => by
   151	      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
   152	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   153	      all_goals rfl
   154	  | .BA'', A => by
   155	      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
   156	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
   157	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
   158	        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   159	      all_goals rfl
   160	  | .BB', A => by
   161	      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
   162	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
   163	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
   164	        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   165	      all_goals rfl
   166	  | .AB'', A => by
   167	      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
   168	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   169	      all_goals rfl
   170	
   171	set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
   172	/-- A placement preserves positivity. -/
   173	theorem place_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   174	    ∀ (p : Placement) {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)}, 0 ≤ A →
   175	      0 ≤ S.place p A
   176	  | .AA', A, hA => by
   177	      classical
   178	      rw [place_AA'_eq]
   179	      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA
   180	        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg))
   181	  | .BA'', A, hA => by
   182	      classical
   183	      rw [place_BA''_eq]
   184	      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
   185	        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
   186	        (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)))
   187	  | .BB', A, hA => by
   188	      classical
   189	      rw [place_BB'_eq]
   190	      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
   191	        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)

     3	/-!
     4	# Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction
     5	
     6	This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
     7	procedure of the sub-line lemma. First, for independent uniform inputs `y` in
     8	the ambient coordinate space and `t` in the scalar field, the point
     9	`lineRepMap v y + t • v` is uniform. This map on ambient-point--parameter pairs
    10	has fibers of size `q`: for nonzero `v`, `y` varies over a coset of the span of
    11	`v`, while its canonical representative and `t` are fixed; for zero `v`, `y`
    12	is fixed and `t` is free. Second, the two coordinate
    13	blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
    14	corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
    15	carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
    16	coordinates.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    21	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    23	The canonical representative map is blueprint
    24	`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
    25	blueprint `def:combine-map`.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    33	
    34	noncomputable section
    35	
    36	/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
    37	
    38	/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
    39	`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
    40	is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    42	-/
    43	theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    44	    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
    45	  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
    46	  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
    47	  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
    48	  exact h.symm
    49	
    50	/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
    51	
    52	/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
    53	canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
    54	the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
    55	`q` elements in the ambient-point--parameter domain: for a nonzero direction
    56	the parameter and canonical representative are determined, while the input
    57	point varies over a coset of the span of the direction. For the zero direction
    58	the input point is fixed and the parameter is free. Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    60	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul {K : Type*} [Field K]
    61	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) :
    62	    (uniformDistribution ((Fin m → K) × K)).map
    63	        (fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) =
    64	      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
    65	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card K) fun x => ?_
    66	  by_cases hv : v = 0
    67	  · subst hv
    68	    have hfilter :
    69	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    70	            fun w => lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) w.1 + w.2 • (0 : Fin m → K)
    71	              = x)
    72	          = ({x} : Finset (Fin m → K)) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset K) := by
    73	      ext w
    74	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
    75	        Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton, and_true, smul_zero,
    76	        add_zero, lineRepMap_zero_apply]
    77	    rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
    78	    simp
    79	  · have hinj : Function.Injective
    80	        (fun c : K => (lineRepMap v x + c • v, directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    81	      intro c₁ c₂ hc
    82	      have hc' : c₁ • v = c₂ • v := by
    83	        have h := congrArg Prod.fst hc
    84	        simpa using h
    85	      have hsub : (c₁ - c₂) • v = 0 := by
    86	        rw [sub_smul, hc', sub_self]
    87	      rcases smul_eq_zero.mp hsub with h | h
    88	      · exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
    89	      · exact absurd h hv
    90	    have himg :
    91	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    92	            fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v = x)
    93	          = (Finset.univ : Finset K).image
    94	              (fun c => (lineRepMap v x + c • v,
    95	                directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    96	      ext w
    97	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image]
    98	      constructor
    99	      · intro hw
   100	        have hrep : lineRepMap v w.1 = lineRepMap v x := by
   101	          rw [← hw, lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   102	        have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + w.2 • v := by
   103	          rw [← hrep]
   104	          exact hw.symm
   105	        have ht : directLineRepParameter v x = w.2 :=
   106	          directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv hx
   107	        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp
   108	          (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v w.1)
   109	        refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   110	        have hw1 : lineRepMap v x + c • v = w.1 := by
   111	          rw [← hrep, hc]
   112	          abel
   113	        rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   114	        exact ⟨hw1, ht⟩
   115	      · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
   116	        show lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v x + c • v) +
   117	          directLineRepParameter v x • v = x
   118	        rw [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   119	        exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v x).symm
   120	    rw [himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj, Finset.card_univ]

   235	theorem embX_val (m : ℕ) (i : Fin m) : (embX m i).val = i.val := rfl

   238	coordinate.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
   239	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

   260	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   262	    {b d x : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd}

   279	    {x : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K} (hx : x ∈ linePoints b d) :

   281	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := hx
   282	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hd
   283	  rw [linePoints_eq_of_mem _ dX (projX b)
   284	    (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap dX (projX b))]
   285	  refine ⟨t * c, ?_⟩
   286	  rw [projX_add, projX_smul, ← hc]
   287	  module

   290	canonical representative of the `Z` block of the base, as soon as the `Z`
   291	block of the direction is a multiple of the source direction.  Blueprint
   292	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   293	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   294	theorem projZ_mem_linePoints {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   295	    (b d : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (dZ : Fin m → K)
   296	    (hd : projZ d ∈ Submodule.span K ({dZ} : Set (Fin m → K)))

   305	  module

   310	field carries an elementary coordinate direction to the elementary coordinate
   311	direction at the same coordinate.  Blueprint
   312	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   315	    (k : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m) :
   316	    directPointToPauli P (coordinateDirection k) = coordinateDirection k := by
   317	  funext j
   318	  simp [directPointToPauli, coordinateDirection, Pi.single_apply]
   319	
   320	/-- Incidence of the `X` blocks: if a source line has as base the canonical
   321	representative, in its own direction, of the `X` block of the base of an
   322	extended line, and if the `X` block of the direction of the extended line
   323	lies in the span of the source direction, then the `X` block of every point
   324	of the extended line is a point of the source line.  Blueprint
   325	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   326	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   327	theorem projX_mem_pointSet (P : AdmissibleParams)
   328	    (base dir : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   329	    (lineX : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   330	    (hbase : lineX.base =
   331	      lineRepMap lineX.direction (projX (directPointToPauli P base)))

     3	/-!
     4	# Coordinate blocks of a truncated extended direction
     5	
     6	This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
     7	diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended
     8	vector by zeroing the coordinates that precede the stored coordinate index,
     9	so each source block is again a prefix truncation: when the stored index is
    10	the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,
    11	preceding blocks vanish, and later blocks remain untruncated.
    12	The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
    13	the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
    14	two identified scalar fields.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The block computations support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The truncation is the prefix restriction of blueprint
    22	`def:ld-question-distribution`; the coordinate blocks are those of
    23	blueprint `def:combine-map`.
    24	-/

    26	open scoped BigOperators
    27	
    28	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    29	
    30	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-! ## Truncation at the first coordinate -/
    35	
    36	/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding the first coordinate changes nothing.
    37	Blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    39	-/
    40	theorem prefixProjection_of_val_zero {L : LdParams} {i : Fin L.m}
    41	    (hi : i.val = 0) (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
    42	    prefixProjection i v = v := by
    43	  funext j
    44	  simp [prefixProjection, hi]
    45	
    46	/-! ## The `X` block of a truncated extended direction -/
    47	
    48	/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at an `X`-block
    49	coordinate is the `X` block truncated at that coordinate of the source space.
    50	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    51	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    52	theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    53	    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    54	    projX (directPointToPauli P
    55	        (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) v)) =
    56	      prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i (projX (directPointToPauli P v)) := by
    57	  funext a
    58	  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
    59	      (if (embX P.m a).val < (embX P.m i).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    60	    if a.val < i.val then 0 else extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embX P.m a))
    61	  rw [embX_val, embX_val]
    62	  by_cases h : a.val < i.val
    63	  · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, map_zero]
    64	  · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]

    67	coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

    72	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m i) v)) = 0 := by
    73	  funext a
    74	  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt
    75	  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
    76	      (if (embX P.m a).val < (embZ P.m i).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    77	    (0 : PauliScalar P)

    81	coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    83	theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar (P : AdmissibleParams)
    84	    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    85	    projX (directPointToPauli P
    86	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by
    87	  funext a
    88	  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt
    89	  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
    90	      (if (embX P.m a).val < (alphaVar P.m).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =

   100	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by

   102	  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt

   113	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   122	    if a.val < i.val then 0 else extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embZ P.m a))

   124	  by_cases h : a.val < i.val
   125	  · rw [if_pos (by omega), if_pos h, map_zero]

     4	/-!
     5	# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
     6	
     7	This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
     8	the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
     9	is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
    10	coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
    11	the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
    12	point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
    13	commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
    14	canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
    15	field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
    16	the same three coordinate ranges.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    21	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    23	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    24	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open scoped BigOperators
    28	
    29	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    30	
    31	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    32	
    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	/-! ## Linearity of the coordinate blocks -/
    36	
    37	/-- The `X` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    38	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	theorem projX_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    41	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    42	    projX (u + v) = projX u + projX v := rfl
    43	
    44	/-- The `Z` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    45	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	theorem projZ_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    48	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    49	    projZ (u + v) = projZ u + projZ v := rfl
    50	
    51	/-- The `X` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    52	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    54	theorem projX_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    55	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    56	    projX (t • u) = t • projX u := rfl
    57	
    58	/-- The `Z` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    59	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    61	theorem projZ_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    62	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    63	    projZ (t • u) = t • projZ u := rfl
    64	
    65	/-! ## The coordinate blocks of an extended point -/
    66	
    67	/-- Split an extended point into its two source point blocks and its two
    68	scalar coordinates.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	def extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    71	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    72	      ((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    73	          (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
    74	        (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :=
    75	  (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCombineEquiv P.m)
    76	      (Equiv.refl (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).trans
    77	    ((Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _).trans
    78	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.refl _)))
    79	
    80	/-- The first block of the decomposition is the `X` block. -/
    81	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX (P : AdmissibleParams)
    82	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    83	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.1 = projX u := by
    84	  funext i
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- The second block of the decomposition is the `Z` block. -/
    88	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams)
    89	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    90	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.2 = projZ u := by
    91	  funext i
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The first scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `alpha`. -/
    95	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_alpha (P : AdmissibleParams)
    96	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    97	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 0 = u (alphaVar P.m) := rfl
    98	
    99	/-- The second scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `beta`. -/
   100	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_beta (P : AdmissibleParams)
   101	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   102	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 1 = u (betaVar P.m) := rfl
   103	
   104	/-- The block decomposition of an extended point carries the uniform law to
   105	the uniform law.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	theorem uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   108	    (uniformDistribution
   109	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   110	        (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) =
   111	      uniformDistribution
   112	        (((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
   113	            (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
   114	          (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) :=
   115	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   116	
   117	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly sampled extended point are
   118	independent and uniform.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   120	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   121	    (uniformDistribution
   122	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   123	        (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)) =
   124	      Distribution.prod
   125	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   126	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) := by
   127	  have hfun :
   128	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   129	          (projX u, projZ u)) =
   130	        fun u => (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1 := by
   131	    funext u
   132	    rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   133	    exact ⟨(extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX P u).symm,
   134	      (extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ P u).symm⟩
   135	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) Prod.fst,
   136	    uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv,
   137	    uniformDistribution_map_fst, uniformDistribution_prod]
   138	
   139	/-! ## Transport to the source scalar field -/
   140	
   141	/-- The `X` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   142	is the transport of its `X` block.  Blueprint
   143	`def:combine-map`, paper
   144	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   145	theorem projX_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   146	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   147	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) =
   148	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projX u i) := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- The `Z` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   151	is the transport of its `Z` block.  Blueprint
   152	`def:combine-map`, paper
   153	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   154	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   155	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   156	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) =
   157	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projZ u i) := rfl
   158	
   159	/-! ## The blocks of an extended direct sample -/
   160	
   161	/-- The stored index, point block and direction block of a uniformly sampled
   162	direct low-degree vector are independent and uniform.  Blueprint
   163	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   165	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   166	    (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map (directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D) =
   167	      uniformDistribution
   168	        (Fin D.m ×
   169	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))) :=
   170	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   171	
   172	/-! ## Compatibility data read off the coordinate blocks -/
   173	
   174	/-- An extended line is compatible with two source lines as soon as each of
   175	its two point blocks is an affine reparameterization of the corresponding
   176	source line: the base block is a point of the source line and the direction
   177	block is a multiple of the source direction.  The two scalar coordinates of
   178	the compatibility data are the `alpha` and `beta` coordinates of the extended
   179	base and direction.  This supplies the domain condition preceding Equation
   180	`eq:combine-lines` in blueprint
   181	`def:combine-map`, paper
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   183	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   184	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K) (aX bX aZ bZ : K)
   185	    (hX : projX u = uX + aX • vX) (hXv : projX v = bX • vX)
   186	    (hZ : projZ u = uZ + aZ • vZ) (hZv : projZ v = bZ • vZ) :
   187	    IsCombineLineCompatible u v uX vX uZ vZ aX bX aZ bZ
   188	      (u (alphaVar m)) (v (alphaVar m)) (u (betaVar m)) (v (betaVar m)) := by
   189	  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun t => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
   190	  · rw [projX_add, projX_smul, hX, hXv]
   191	    module
   192	  · rw [projZ_add, projZ_smul, hZ, hZv]
   193	    module
   194	
   195	/-- An extended line whose two source lines carry the inherited direction
   196	blocks is compatible with them, with both affine reparameterizations the
   197	identity.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   199	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_inherited {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   200	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
   201	    IsCombineLineCompatible u v (projX u) (projX v) (projZ u) (projZ v)
   202	      0 1 0 1 (u (alphaVar m)) (v (alphaVar m)) (u (betaVar m))
   203	      (v (betaVar m)) :=
   204	  isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks u v _ _ _ _ 0 1 0 1
   205	    (by module) (by module) (by module) (by module)
   206	
   207	end
   208	
   209	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLinePrefix
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
     5	
     6	The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
     7	the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
     8	scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
     9	coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
    10	of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
    11	This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
    12	source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
    13	reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
    14	line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
    15	same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    20	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    21	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    22	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    23	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	open scoped BigOperators
    27	
    28	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    29	
    30	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-! ## The identification of the two scalar fields as a bijection -/
    35	
    36	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    37	source scalar field on one source block, presented as a bijection.  Blueprint
    38	`def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	noncomputable def directBlockToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    41	    (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃ (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) where
    42	  toFun v := fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v i)
    43	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    44	  left_inv v := by
    45	    funext i
    46	    simp
    47	  right_inv v := by
    48	    funext i
    49	    simp
    50	
    51	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    52	source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
    53	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    55	noncomputable def directPointToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    56	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    57	      (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) where
    58	  toFun := directPointToPauli P
    59	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    60	  left_inv v := by
    61	    funext i
    62	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    63	  right_inv v := by
    64	    funext i
    65	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    66	
    67	/-- The `X` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `X`
    68	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	theorem projX_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    72	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projX u) := rfl
    73	
    74	/-- The `Z` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `Z`
    75	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    77	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    78	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    79	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projZ u) := rfl
    80	
    81	/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
    82	
    83	/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field
    84	is uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    85	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    86	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (uniformDistribution
    88	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    89	        (directPointToPauli P) =
    90	      uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) :=
    91	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directPointToPauliEquiv P)
    92	
    93	/-- A uniformly random source block transported to the source scalar field is
    94	uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    96	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directBlockToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    97	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    98	        (fun v => directBlockToPauliEquiv P v) =
    99	      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :=
   100	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   101	
   102	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly random extended point, read in the
   103	source scalar field, are independent and uniformly random.  Blueprint
   104	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   106	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   107	    (uniformDistribution
   108	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   109	        (fun u => (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   110	          projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   111	      Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   112	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   113	  classical
   114	  have hfun :
   115	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   116	          (projX (directPointToPauli P u), projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   117	        fun u => (Equiv.prodCongr (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   118	          (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)) (projX u, projZ u) := rfl
   119	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)),
   120	    uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ, ← uniformDistribution_prod,
   121	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv, uniformDistribution_prod]
   122	
   123	/-! ## Resampling a uniform point along a line -/
   124	
   125	/-- Reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on
   126	the line through the canonical representative, in a fixed direction, of a
   127	uniformly random point is the same as reading that function at a uniformly
   128	random point.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   130	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul_comp {K : Type*} [Field K]
   131	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} {γ : Type*} [DecidableEq γ]
   132	    (v : Fin m → K) (g : (Fin m → K) → γ) :
   133	    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K))
   134	          (uniformDistribution K)).map
   135	        (fun w => g (lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v)) =
   136	      (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K)).map g := by
   137	  classical
   138	  rw [← uniformDistribution_prod,
   139	    ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun w : (Fin m → K) × K =>
   140	      lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) g,
   141	    uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul]
   142	
   143	end
   144	
   145	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineTransport
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# The branch data of the sub-line sampling procedure
     5	
     6	The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma draws a line kind, a stored
     7	extended coordinate, and an unrestricted extended direction, and forms from
     8	them the direction of the extended line: the elementary direction at the
     9	stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with the
    10	coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the diagonal
    11	branch.  The two source lines are then read off the two coordinate blocks.
    12	This module fixes the coordinate index that each source line must carry: the
    13	stored coordinate itself when it belongs to that block, the first coordinate
    14	otherwise.  With that choice the source block of the extended direction always
    15	lies in the line spanned by the corresponding source direction, which is the
    16	incidence hypothesis of the two projection lemmas.  The module also records
    17	that moving an extended point to its canonical representative does not change
    18	the canonical representative of either of its source blocks.
    19	
    20	## References
    21	
    22	The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    23	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    25	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    26	445--480, paper lines 970--989; the prefix truncation is that of
    27	blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`.
    28	-/
    29	
    30	open scoped BigOperators
    31	
    32	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    33	
    34	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    35	
    36	noncomputable section
    37	
    38	/-! ## The three ranges of extended coordinates -/
    39	
    40	/-- Every extended coordinate is an `X`-block coordinate, a `Z`-block
    41	coordinate, or one of the two scalar coordinates.  Blueprint
    42	`def:combine-map`, paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    44	theorem extendedCoordinate_cases (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 * m + 2)) :
    45	    (∃ i : Fin m, k = embX m i) ∨ (∃ j : Fin m, k = embZ m j) ∨
    46	      k = alphaVar m ∨ k = betaVar m := by
    47	  rcases lt_or_ge k.val m with hk | hk
    48	  · exact Or.inl ⟨⟨k.val, hk⟩, Fin.ext (embX_val m ⟨k.val, hk⟩).symm⟩
    49	  · rcases lt_or_ge k.val (2 * m) with hk2 | hk2
    50	    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨⟨k.val - m, by omega⟩, Fin.ext ?_⟩)
    51	      rw [embZ_val]
    52	      change k.val = m + (k.val - m)
    53	      omega
    54	    · have hk3 : k.val < 2 * m + 2 := k.isLt
    55	      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge k.val (2 * m + 1) with hk4 | hk4
    56	      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl (Fin.ext ?_)))
    57	        rw [alphaVar_val]
    58	        omega
    59	      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Fin.ext ?_)))
    60	        rw [betaVar_val]
    61	        omega
    62	
    63	/-! ## Linearity of the identification of the two scalar fields -/
    64	
    65	/-- The identification of the two scalar fields is additive on extended
    66	points.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    68	theorem directPointToPauli_add (P : AdmissibleParams)
    69	    (u v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    70	    directPointToPauli P (u + v) =
    71	      directPointToPauli P u + directPointToPauli P v := by
    72	  funext i
    73	  simp [directPointToPauli]
    74	
    75	/-- The identification of the two scalar fields carries a scalar multiple of
    76	an extended point to the multiple by the identified scalar.  Blueprint
    77	`def:combine-map`, paper
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    79	theorem directPointToPauli_smul (P : AdmissibleParams)
    80	    (t : DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
    81	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    82	    directPointToPauli P (t • u) =
    83	      extendedDirectScalarEquiv P t • directPointToPauli P u := by
    84	  funext i
    85	  simp [directPointToPauli]
    86	
    87	/-! ## The coordinate index carried by each source line -/
    88	
    89	/-- The first coordinate of the source space.  Blueprint
    90	`eq:chi-func`, paper
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    92	-/
    93	def subLineFirstIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fin P.m :=
    94	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.one_le_m⟩
    95	
    96	/-- The coordinate index carried by the source `X` line of a branch: the
    97	stored extended coordinate when it is an `X`-block coordinate, and the first
    98	coordinate otherwise.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	def subLineXIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) : Fin P.m :=
   101	  if h : k.val < P.m then ⟨k.val, h⟩ else subLineFirstIndex P
   102	
   103	/-- The coordinate index carried by the source `Z` line of a branch: the
   104	stored extended coordinate when it is a `Z`-block coordinate, and the first
   105	coordinate otherwise.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	def subLineZIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) : Fin P.m :=
   108	  if h : P.m ≤ k.val ∧ k.val < 2 * P.m then ⟨k.val - P.m, by omega⟩
   109	  else subLineFirstIndex P
   110	
   111	/-- At an `X`-block coordinate the source `X` line carries that coordinate. -/
   112	theorem subLineXIndex_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   113	    subLineXIndex P (embX P.m i) = i := by
   114	  have h : (embX P.m i).val < P.m := by
   115	    rw [embX_val]
   116	    exact i.isLt
   117	  rw [subLineXIndex, dif_pos h]
   118	  exact Fin.ext (embX_val P.m i)
   119	
   120	/-- At a `Z`-block coordinate the source `X` line carries the first
   121	coordinate. -/
   122	theorem subLineXIndex_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (j : Fin P.m) :
   123	    subLineXIndex P (embZ P.m j) = subLineFirstIndex P := by

   190	/-- The direction of the extended line of a branch: the elementary direction
   191	at the stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with
   192	the coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the
   193	diagonal branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   194	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   195	def subLineExtDirection (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   196	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2))
   197	    (w : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   198	    Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd :=
   199	  match kind with
   200	  | .axis => coordinateDirection k
   201	  | .diagonal => directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) k w
   202	
   203	/-- The direction of a source line of a branch: the elementary direction at
   204	its coordinate index in the axis branch, and the given source block with the
   205	coordinates preceding that index replaced by zero in the diagonal branch.
   206	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   207	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   208	def subLineSourceDirection (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   209	    (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   210	  match kind with
   211	  | .axis => coordinateDirection i
   212	  | .diagonal => prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i v

   214	/-! ## Incidence of the two source blocks of a branch direction -/
   215	
   216	/-- The `X` block of the direction of the extended line of a branch lies in
   217	the line spanned by the direction of its source `X` line.  Blueprint
   218	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   219	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   220	theorem projX_subLineExtDirection_mem_span (P : AdmissibleParams)
   221	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2))
   222	    (w : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   223	    projX (directPointToPauli P (subLineExtDirection P kind k w)) ∈
   224	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P)
   225	        ({subLineSourceDirection P kind (subLineXIndex P k)
   226	          (projX (directPointToPauli P w))} :
   227	          Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   228	  rcases extendedCoordinate_cases P.m k with ⟨i, rfl⟩ | ⟨j, rfl⟩ | rfl | rfl <;>
   229	    cases kind
   230	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   231	        (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) =
   232	        (coordinateDirection i : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) := by
   233	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   234	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_embX i
   235	    rw [subLineXIndex_embX]
   236	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   237	      (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) ∈ _
   238	    rw [hval]
   239	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   240	  · rw [subLineXIndex_embX]
   241	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   242	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) w)) ∈ _
   243	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_embX]
   244	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   245	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   246	        (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) = 0 := by
   247	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   248	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_embZ j
   249	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   250	      (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) ∈ _
   251	    rw [hval]
   252	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   253	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   254	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m j) w)) ∈ _
   255	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_embZ]
   256	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   257	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   258	        (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   259	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   260	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_alphaVar
   261	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   262	      (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   263	    rw [hval]
   264	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   265	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   266	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   267	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar]
   268	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   269	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   270	        (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   271	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   272	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_betaVar
   273	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   274	      (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   275	    rw [hval]
   276	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   277	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   278	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   279	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_betaVar]
   280	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _

   286	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper

   320	      exact projZ_coordinateDirection_embZ j

   322	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   323	      (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) ∈ _
   324	    rw [hval]
   325	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _

   332	        (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) = 0 := by

   336	      (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) ∈ _

   356	/-! ## Canonical representatives of the two source blocks -/
   357	
   358	/-- Replacing an extended point by its canonical representative in the
   359	direction of the extended line does not change the canonical representative
   360	of its `X` block in the direction of the source `X` line, as soon as the `X`
   361	block of the extended direction lies in the line spanned by the source
   362	direction.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   363	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   364	theorem lineRepMap_projX_directPointToPauli_lineRepMap (P : AdmissibleParams)
   365	    (v x : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   366	    (dX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   367	    (hdir : projX (directPointToPauli P v) ∈
   368	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P) ({dX} : Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) :
   369	    lineRepMap dX (projX (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x))) =
   370	      lineRepMap dX (projX (directPointToPauli P x)) := by
   371	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v x)
   372	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hdir
   373	  have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + t • v := by
   374	    rw [ht]
   375	    abel
   376	  have hstep : projX (directPointToPauli P x) =
   377	      projX (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x)) +
   378	        (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P t * c) • dX := by
   379	    conv_lhs => rw [hx]
   380	    rw [directPointToPauli_add, directPointToPauli_smul, projX_add, projX_smul,
   381	      ← hc]
   382	    module
   383	  rw [hstep, lineRepMap_add_smul]
   384	
   385	/-- Replacing an extended point by its canonical representative in the
   386	direction of the extended line does not change the canonical representative
   387	of its `Z` block in the direction of the source `Z` line, as soon as the `Z`
   388	block of the extended direction lies in the line spanned by the source
   389	direction.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   390	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   391	theorem lineRepMap_projZ_directPointToPauli_lineRepMap (P : AdmissibleParams)
   392	    (v x : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   393	    (dZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   394	    (hdir : projZ (directPointToPauli P v) ∈
   395	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P) ({dZ} : Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) :
   396	    lineRepMap dZ (projZ (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x))) =
   397	      lineRepMap dZ (projZ (directPointToPauli P x)) := by
   398	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v x)
   399	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hdir
   400	  have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + t • v := by
   401	    rw [ht]

   403	  have hstep : projZ (directPointToPauli P x) =
   404	      projZ (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x)) +
   405	        (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P t * c) • dZ := by

   407	    rw [directPointToPauli_add, directPointToPauli_smul, projZ_add, projZ_smul,

     5	/-!
     6	# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
     9	for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`.
    67	-/
    68	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    69	  q := P.q
    70	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    71	  d := P.d
    72	  k := 1
    73	  hm := by omega
    74	  hd := P.hd
    75	  hk := by decide
    76	  hq := P.hq
    77	
    78	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    79	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    80	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    81	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    82	  index : Fin D.m
    83	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    84	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    85	
    86	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    87	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    88	
    89	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    90	coordinates. -/
    91	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    92	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    93	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    94	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    95	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    96	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    97	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    98	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	
   100	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   101	independent coordinates. -/
   102	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   103	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   104	      Fin D.m ×
   105	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   106	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   107	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   108	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   109	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   110	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	
   112	/-- Compatibility name for the index-first direct-sample decomposition. -/
   113	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   114	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   115	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   116	  directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D
   117	
   118	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   119	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   120	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   121	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   122	
   123	/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding a prefix index is idempotent: the
   124	coordinates it leaves unchanged are exactly those it does not zero. -/
   125	theorem directPrefixProjection_idem (D : DirectLdParams) (i : Fin D.m)
   126	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   127	    directPrefixProjection i (directPrefixProjection i v) =
   128	      directPrefixProjection i v := by
   129	  funext j
   130	  unfold directPrefixProjection
   131	  split_ifs <;> rfl
